title: Jensen Huang, Nvidia and the risks that come with ‘boomerang bosses’
headline: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia highlights corporate governance and key person risks
summary: Following a brief departure due to personal conduct issues, co-founder Jensen Huang has returned as CEO of Nvidia. The high-profile leadership transition exposed Nvidia's heavy dependency on Huang, illustrating severe key person risk for a critical player in the global artificial intelligence sector. While financial markets reacted positively to his reinstatement, academic research on boomerang executives indicates ongoing challenges regarding firm governance and oversight.
why_it_matters: Organisations heavily reliant on individual founders or leaders for AI development must manage acute key person risk by strengthening corporate governance and oversight structures.

quotes.text: The idea of “key person risk” is the vulnerability from depending heavily on one person whose absence could severely disrupt how a business works.
What is likely to be a longer term worry is issues of reputation and governance at the world’s most important chip-maker.

classification.significance_reason: Highlights major governance and key person vulnerabilities at a central AI infrastructure firm, though it is primarily commentary rather than regulatory policy.
